title.value: Optimal Transport for Unsupervised Hallucination Detection in Neural Machine Translation
title.justification: The paper mainly addresses the issue of hallucination detection in neural machine translation, referring to the use of Optimal Transport as a method for unsupervised detection. This is clearly stated in the title.
title.quote: Optimal Transport for Unsupervised Hallucination Detection in Neural Machine Translation

extractions.description: The paper addresses the problem of hallucination detection in Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models, introducing an unsupervised approach using optimal transport (OT) to identify anomalous attention patterns. It proposes a detector that identifies statistically different cross-attention patterns indicative of hallucinations, showing improved performance over existing methods. The proposed approach can be applied to any attention-based NMT model, leveraging the optimal transport formulation to capture irregular patterns in source attention mass distributions independent of the translation quality.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving neural machine translation by addressing hallucination detection through optimal transport methods. It doesn't directly address climate or ecological sustainable development issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this paper, we address the problem of hallucination detection in NMT by following a simple intuition: as hallucinations are detached from the source content, they exhibit cross-attention patterns that are statistically different from those of good quality translations.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses purely on improving the technical quality and reliability of Neural Machine Translation systems rather than any direct applications related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we address the problem of hallucination detection in NMT by following a simple intuition: as hallucinations are detached from the source content, they exhibit cross-attention patterns that are statistically different from those of good quality translations.

secondary_categories.quote: Neural machine translation (NMT) has become the de-facto standard in real-world machine translation applications. However, NMT models can unpredictably produce severely pathological translations, known as hallucinations.

primary_sub_category.quote: We propose an OT-inspired fully unsupervised hallucination detector that can be plugged into any attention-based NMT model.

secondary_sub_categories.quote: Experimental results show that our detector not only outperforms all previous model-based detectors, but is also competitive with detectors that employ external models trained on millions of samples for related tasks such as quality estimation and cross-lingual sentence similarity.

applications.quote: We frame this problem with an optimal transport formulation and propose a fully unsupervised, plug-in detector that can be used with any attention-based NMT model.
